result:
Confirmed: `spec-assets/` and `SPEC.md` are untouched, `vite.config.ts` unchanged. Only `Info.plist`, `Transcribe.vue`, and the new `app/assets/sample.wav` (a bundled copy, not a modification of the read-only source) changed.

## Summary

Implemented SPEC.md §5 (Transcribe/Speech):

- **`app/assets/sample.wav`** — copy of `spec-assets/sample.wav` placed under the project's existing asset-bundling convention (`app/assets/` → auto-copied into the app bundle by the Vite build).
- **`App_Resources/iOS/Info.plist`** — added `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`.
- **`app/components/Transcribe.vue`** — wired to `SFSpeechRecognizer`/`SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest`: authorization status/request, enable/disable logic, live partial-transcript streaming, `Completed in N.N s` timing, and error surfacing on failure — all matching the exact labels in §5.

`ns build ios` succeeds. I also ran the app live in the iOS Simulator (idb-driven) and verified the full flow end-to-end: request → grant → live streaming partial transcript → final transcript matching `reference-transcript.txt` (>90% word overlap) → `Completed in 1.4 s`; and the deny path (`Speech access: denied`, button stays disabled, no crash).

One note: the pre-existing booted simulator was on iOS 26.5, where Apple's local speech-recognition daemon in that (beta) Simulator runtime fails with a native `kAFAssistantErrorDomain Code=1101` error — our error-surfacing code correctly displayed this instead of crashing, but I couldn't get real transcription there. I created a temporary iOS 18.5 simulator to confirm the app works correctly end-to-end (transcription succeeds), then deleted that temporary simulator afterward. This is an OS/Simulator-runtime limitation, not an app defect.
